In combat, a Beast shares your Initiative|XPHB count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

Shared Spirit.

entriesHtml:

You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

Daunt.

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, make a Charisma (Intimidation) check and choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your Intimidation check. On a failed save, the creature has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the Frightened creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against this effect.

You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

You manage your Beast better than many. You gain the following benefits.

Reining the Beast.

When you would be affected by the The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger of your Beast feature, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to immediately end the effect.

You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

name: The Kiss
entriesHtml:
Your bite is intoxicating to your prey.

Pleasurable Feeding.

When you feed, you can choose to roll d4s instead of d6s for your Feed Dice. When you do so, you regain 1 Blood Point on a roll of a 4 on the d4, and the creature is Charmed by you. The Charmed condition lasts until the end of your next turn.
description:
Your bite is intoxicating to your prey.

**Pleasurable Feeding**

When you feed, you can choose to roll d4s instead of d6s for your Feed Dice. When you do so, you regain 1 Blood Point on a roll of a 4 on the d4, and the creature is Charmed by you. The Charmed condition lasts until the end of your next turn.

name: Thin-Blooded
entriesHtml:
You have a portion of a vampire's blood flowing in your veins. You are a thin-blood, often destined for a place among the clanless. You gain the following benefits.

Able to Feed.

You feed on the blood of other creatures. This is most often accomplished through your sharp fangs. As an action, you can feed on another creature within 5 feet of yourself if the target is willing, Charmed by you, or has the Incapacitated, Grappled, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious condition. You can feed only once per turn.

You have 2d6 Feed Dice. When you feed, roll up to your maximum Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). The creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total. This damage only reduces the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum by an amount equal to the roll's total. If you roll a 6 on a d6 on a Feed Die, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. If a creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point.

Feeding from the Willing.

If you feed on a willing creature or a creature Charmed by you, it can spend 1 Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die. It rolls the Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die and reduces its Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum by the amount rolled, and you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. Feeding in this way doesn't end the Charmed condition.

Hit Die Deficit.

If a creature has no remaining Hit Point Dice|XPHB, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier, and the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the roll's total.

Maximum Successful Feedings.

A creature can provide a number of Blood Points based on its size. A Small creature provides 1 Blood Point, a Medium provides 3, a Large provides 5, a Huge provides 7, and a Gargantuan provides 10. A creature regains all lost Blood Points when it finishes a Long Rest|XPHB.

Creature Susceptible to Feed.

You can feed on any creature with blood or other life-giving fluid. Work with your GM to determine the types of creatures you can feed on.

Kindred, but Not Kindred.

You ignore the Kindred class prerequisite for choosing Kindred feats|feats|category=kf. You can't gain levels in the Kindred class.

Kindred Vitae.

You have a number of Blood Points equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus minus one.

Supernatural Spellcasting.

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells from your Kindred feats. Your spells require no Verbal or Somatic components, and they require no Material components unless they are consumed by the spell or have a cost specified in it. Taking damage can't break your Concentration|XPHB for spells cast using this feature.

Shadowplay.

name: Well-Read
entriesHtml:
You grew up with your nose buried in books. You gain the following benefits.

Creature Lore.

When you roll Initiative|XPHB, you can recall lore about a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself; you know one Immunity|XPHB, Resistance, Vulnerability|XPHB, or Trait of that creature. You decide when you use this ability.

Font of Useful Knowledge.

When you roll a 1 on an Intelligence (Arcana or History) check, you can reroll the die, and you must use the new roll.

Rare Knowledge.

If you succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana or History) check, you learn additional lore. The GM has final say on what you learn, if anything. The lore might consist of important details, amusing revelations, or even secret lore that has never been widely known. The more information you already know about the thing, the more precise and detailed the information you receive is. That information is accurate but might be couched in figurative language or poetry, as determined by the GM.
